minutes.headline: School Committee held a 75-minute finalist interview with Brent Conway for superintendent; no hiring vote taken
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee conducted a scripted 75-minute finalist interview of superintendent candidate Brent Conway, currently assistant superintendent at Pentucket Regional. Conway answered 13 prepared questions on budget process, leadership, student safety, hiring, staff culture and stakeholder relationships, and named budget stability, student support systems, and community connection as his top three entry priorities. The only vote taken was a roll-call motion to adjourn; no decision on the superintendent selection was made at this meeting.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Beardmore/Bazowski yes, Mbo yes, Skully yes, chair yes)

budget_items.what_was_said: Conway said Lunenburg's state aid has been declining, shifting more of the cost to local taxpayers, and compared it to Pentucket's own decline in state aid share over ten years.

budget_items.topic: Pentucket budget gap closed via new revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: Conway described facing a budget gap at Pentucket that was closed partly by raising revenue through summer programming, expanded preschool, and increased facility rental income.
Conway said putting the transportation contract out to competitive bid brought the three-year contract cost down sharply once a competitor entered the bidding.
Conway called health insurance a major budget driver, citing recent rate increases well above typical assumed growth rates.
Conway explained that an approved September budget commonly looks different by year-end because of line transfers made to respond to changing needs, such as adding a kindergarten class.
Conway said UGGA has remained largely flat and argued that if it kept pace with Chapter 70 growth the town would have more budget flexibility.
Conway described a robotics program he built at Pentucket that runs on an annual budget funded largely by industry sponsorships and grants rather than district funds.

budget_items.topic: School budget share of total town budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Conway noted the schools' share of the town budget rose after last year's override and is coming back down, and cited other towns' target school/town budget split ratios as points of comparison.

what_happened.line: School Committee interviewed superintendent finalist Brent Conway for 75 minutes; no hiring vote was taken.
Conway, assistant superintendent at Pentucket Regional, answered set questions on budgeting, leadership, safety and hiring.
Conway said state aid has been declining and shifting more cost onto local taxpayers, drawing a comparison to Pentucket.
Conway named budget stability, student support systems and community connection as his top entry priorities.
The only recorded vote was a roll call to adjourn the meeting.

why_it_matters: This is one step in the process of choosing the district's next superintendent, whose priorities will shape budget requests residents later vote on.
Conway's comments on state aid and local cost-shifting touch the same revenue question that affects the town's tax bill each budget cycle.
No decision was made here; a hiring vote at a later meeting is what changes district leadership.
